assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
caveats: Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once; duplicates were removed in the clean view, keeping the first ingestion.

Volume spike 18 Oct–31 Oct: attempt volume was +39% versus the usual level for those weekdays over 14 days. Real business events (sales) and data gaps both look like this, so check before comparing totals across this period. It is flagged for context and is not a data error by itself.

facts.text: The scan of October 2026 payment data raised 2 findings: one warning (duplicate records) and one informational item (volume spike).
On 12 Oct, 341 attempts were ingested twice: 11,704 raw rows versus 11,363 unique attempts, about 3.0% extra rows.
The duplicates were removed in the clean view, keeping the first ingestion of each attempt, so each attempt is counted once.
From 18 Oct to 31 Oct, attempt volume was 39% above the usual level for those weekdays, over 14 days.

response.headline: October's data has one real quality problem: 341 duplicate attempts on 12 Oct, already removed. There is also an unusual volume spike from 18 Oct, which is not an error by itself.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the marketing/promotions calendar for 18–31 Oct and compare the spike against merchant-level volumes.
hypotheses.rationale: Real sales and data problems both produce volume jumps. The scan flags the spike for context only and does not identify its cause.
hypotheses.text: The 18–31 Oct volume spike may reflect a genuine business event such as a sale or campaign rather than a data gap or error.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Review ingestion job logs for 12 Oct for retries or double loads.
hypotheses.rationale: The duplicates are confined to a single day, which is typical of a one-off ingestion repeat, but the scan does not show the cause.
hypotheses.text: The 12 Oct duplicates may come from a re-run or replay of an ingestion job on that day.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The duplicates on 12 Oct were removed in the clean view.
recommendations.rationale: Raw rows overstate 12 Oct volume by 341 attempts (about 3.0%).
recommendations.text: Use the clean view (not the raw table) for all October reporting so the 12 Oct duplicates are not double-counted.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The 18–31 Oct volume spike may reflect a genuine business event.
recommendations.rationale: A spike from a sale and one from a data gap look the same in the numbers, and they should be interpreted differently.
recommendations.text: Confirm the cause of the 18–31 Oct volume spike with the business team before comparing totals across that period.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The 12 Oct duplicates may come from a re-run or replay of an ingestion job.
recommendations.rationale: Preventing repeat ingestion avoids relying on downstream clean-up.
recommendations.text: Ask the data engineering team to investigate the 12 Oct double ingestion and add a duplicate check at load time.
